entities.label: EventWindow
entities.summary:
The Battle of Nicopolis, fought on September 25, 1396, was a decisive Ottoman victory that ended the Crusader siege of the fortress of Nicopolis. This pivotal event marked a turning point in the Balkans, as the Ottomans expanded their control over the region. The battle was a culmination of a series of conflicts between the Ottoman Empire and the Crusader states in the late 14th century.

The Ottomans, led by Sultan Bayezid I, were able to crush the Crusader forces, which were largely composed of French, German, and Burgundian knights. The battle was a significant defeat for the Crusaders, who had been attempting to retake the region from the Ottomans.

The consequences of the Battle of Nicopolis were far-reaching, as it paved the way for the Ottoman conquest of the Balkans and the eventual fall of Constantinople in 1453. The battle also marked a significant shift in the balance of power in Europe, as the Ottoman Empire emerged as a major player in the region.

The legacy of the Battle of Nicopolis can be seen in the continued Ottoman expansion into Europe, which would have significant consequences for the continent in the centuries to come. The battle also marked a turning point in the history of the Crusades, as the Ottomans would go on to become one of the dominant powers in the region.
